why: XLP +3.60 pct to $83.43, first up week after seven down, reclaiming $81.00, the $81.70 double bottom (retested Wed) and the 200D ($82.81) in one Thursday; seventeen of nineteen tracked names rose; the 50D $83.64 is 21 cents overhead (wiki/consumer-staples.md; macro/facts.json).

The regime favors the shelter relatively: UMich 46.3 with current conditions at an all-time low, mortgage 7.40 pct, trade-down inside the store (WMT +6.8 pct, COST September comps +11.4 pct), and calendar-page Ophelia names 'staples with pricing power' as a holding a +0.6 pct headline CPI makes right (wiki/consumer-staples.md; wiki/economic-calendar.md COUNCIL READ; wiki/synthesis.md Wire 5).

The bid was a rotation, not a print: PEP beat and cut its profit guide the same day and ended flat; the staples page's 'wider credit spreads' attribution is not supported by FRED (HY narrowed 324 -> 315); Ophelia stays neutral -- 'a relative trade, not an absolute one' (wiki/consumer-staples.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.A and 7.B.2).

Week RF raised 28 -> 45 and MC 45 -> 48: the fund is back above its Sep 11 level and the week's prints (CPI food-at-home Wed, retail sales Thu, ACI Tue) are two-sided; the favorable band is arithmetic-driven (breadth 90, up-volume 97.7 pct) (wiki/consumer-staples.md).
risks: XLP's 30-day correlation to SPY flipped positive -> negative (+0.095 -> -0.009), the strict-criterion alert (second flip in three weeks, issue opened): statistically a sector with no relationship to the index, not a hedge (wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR CORRELATION MATRIX).

Falsifier: a daily close under $81.70 (Marky's stop); the Thursday rotation 'can reverse the day the AI names stabilize'; a rejection at the 50D with a close under the 20D $82.14 scales out (wiki/consumer-staples.md).

The carry gap is ~-250bp and DXY 102.21 is a fourth weekly gain into PM Oct 21, PG Oct 22, KO/MDLZ Oct 27 -- PEP already put a number on the stronger dollar (wiki/consumer-staples.md; wiki/synthesis.md Wire 7).

why: The sector closed above where it stood four weeks ago ($82.84 on Sep 11) and YTD leads XLY by ~14 pts (+9.5 vs -4.9 pct); month relative momentum 70 is the third-best on the board (wiki/consumer-staples.md; inputs/2026-10-09/consumer_staples.json metrics).

Branded food is the dissent: GIS 2 pct above its 52-week low at a 7.6 pct yield with sales falling in every U.S. unit, CPB -2.1 pct, KMB's lowered outlook; the trade-down is inside the store, not into the sector (wiki/consumer-staples.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 1).

Month RF raised 32 -> 42 and MC held at 45: PM Oct 21, PG Oct 22, KO/MDLZ Oct 27, MO/HSY Oct 29, CL Oct 30 are the three largest staples prints in three days with DXY at 102 translation (wiki/consumer-staples.md EARNINGS CALENDAR).
risks: Guide cuts spread (PEP's cut becomes a pattern at PG, KO, MDLZ on FX and input costs): branded names -5 to -8 pct; the desk's probability 30 pct (wiki/consumer-staples.md RISK SCENARIOS).
Falsifier: breakdown below $80.13 (the prior week low); relief falsifier: 10Y under 5.10 pct with the 50D held turns Ophelia defensive-lean (wiki/consumer-staples.md).
A dollar rally past 102.5 costs the multinationals 2-3 pct extra; the restriction on commodity longs is a separate rule but the same dollar (wiki/consumer-staples.md; wiki/materials.md).

extracts.lead_summary: The shelter got its bid, a week late. XLP rose 3.6% to $83.43 — its first up week after seven straight losses — reclaiming the $81.00 shelf, the $81.70 double bottom and the 200-day ($82.81) in a single Thursday. Seventeen of the nineteen names tracked here rose. Costco's September comp printed +11.4%, PepsiCo beat and then cut its profit guide, Philip Morris closed Friday at a 52-week high, and the 10-year gave back four basis points to 5.24%. I said PepsiCo on Thursday would decide whether $81.00 came back. $81.00 came back — on a rotation out of growth, not on PepsiCo's guide.
